The Muslims ultimately achieved victory, demonstrating that success comes not from numbers but from faith, unity, and reliance upon Allah.

The Prophet ﷺ sent an army of 3,000 companions toward the north after a Muslim envoy was killed. Three commanders were appointed in advance: Zayd ibn Harithah (RA), Jaʿfar ibn Abi Talib (RA), and Abdullah ibn Rawahah (RA).

When the Muslim army reached Muʾtah, they faced an enormous force from the Byzantine Roman army and their allies. Despite the overwhelming odds, the companions showed extraordinary courage.

One after another, the appointed commanders were martyred while holding the banner of Islam. Finally, Khalid ibn al-Walid (RA) took command and used his military skill to safely withdraw the Muslim army.
This episode highlights the bravery of the companions, the sacrifice of the martyrs, and the leadership that preserved the Muslim army.

In the first episode of Life of the Final Messenger ﷺ, Mufti Menk takes us back to the miraculous Year of the Elephant — when Allah protected the Ka‘bah from Abraha’s army — and the divine events that led to the birth of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, the greatest mercy ever sent to mankind.

Witness how Allah shattered arrogance without a single sword being raised, and how this historic moment became the divine prelude to the arrival of the Final Messenger ﷺ — a man destined to guide humanity with mercy, wisdom, and truth.

07:56 Early Blessings & Ḥalīmah al-Saʿdiyyah
